C3-01.title: The signal to go to the net
C3-01.scene: Your crosscourt skimmed the net and dropped in front of the opponent.
C3-01.cue: The opponent bends and swings up from below.
C3-01.question: Where do you go?

answer.why: They're lifting it from below. Move in and take the floater as a volley.
answer.caption: You moved in and volleyed it

lo.why: Safe, but you let the floater bounce and the chance shrinks.
lo.caption: The chance went by

hi.short: All the way to the net at once
hi.why: If you run without stopping, the lob goes over your head. Stop when they hit.
hi.caption: It went over your head

C3-01.coach: When they lift it, that's when you go in.
C3-01.next: Once you're in, how far apart are you two?

C3-02.title: Spacing when you're both up
C3-02.scene: You're both at the net. Your partner's volley went deep down the middle.
C3-02.cue: You and your partner are more than five steps apart.
C3-02.question: Where do you go?

answer.why: With the ball in the middle, the gap between you is the biggest hole. Close it.
answer.caption: You closed the hole

lo.why: Guarding the sideline is right, but you'll both be late on a ball down the middle.
lo.caption: Your partner barely reaches it

hi.why: Our ball went deep — there's no reason to back off. It only makes the hole bigger.
hi.caption: Beaten through the middle

C3-02.coach: Ball in the middle? You both move to the middle.
C3-02.next: How many steps off the net?

C3-03.title: Both up: how far off the net?
C3-03.scene: You both came to the net. You're well behind your partner.
C3-03.cue: The opponent is getting set to hit low and fast.
C3-03.question: Where do you stand?

answer.short: Two or three steps off the net
answer.why: Any closer and you're weak to lobs; any farther and you're weak to balls at your feet. Two or three steps is just right.
answer.caption: You hit down on it

lo.why: Safe against lobs, but you take low balls at your feet.
lo.caption: You barely dig it out

hi.why: With both opponents back, backing off means you can't reach a short ball.
hi.caption: You couldn't reach the short ball

C3-03.coach: When you're both up, stand two or three steps off the net.
C3-03.next: What if the ball is in the corner?

C3-04.title: The ball is in their left corner
C3-04.scene: Our ball went deep into the left corner of their court.
C3-04.cue: Your partner is up near the left sideline; you're front right.
C3-04.question: Where do you go?

answer.why: From the corner, their lanes are narrow. Your partner covers the line; you cover the middle.
answer.caption: You blocked the middle lane

lo.why: Almost nothing comes to the right sideline from that corner. The middle is open.
lo.caption: You chase it late and get it

hi.short: Wide and back on the right
hi.why: Moving away from the ball opens the middle even more. The angles are on the ball's side.
hi.caption: Beaten through the middle

C3-04.coach: Rotate together toward where the ball goes.
C3-04.next: What if a high ball comes?

C3-05.title: A high volley chance
C3-05.scene: The opponent's ball floats up above your shoulder.
C3-05.cue: Their net player is right in front of you.
C3-05.question: Where do you hit it?

answer.why: Hit a high ball down. The nearby net player's feet are the hardest place to dig it out.
answer.caption: Drilled it at their feet

lo.why: Not bad, but the player at the back has time to get it.
lo.caption: The back player gets it

hi.short: A lob volley over the net player
hi.why: Floating a high ball back hands the chance to them.
hi.caption: You got smashed

C3-05.coach: Hit a high volley at the feet of the closest player.

C3-06.title: Both opponents back: where to?
C3-06.scene: Both opponents are holding on at the baseline.
C3-06.cue: The ball comes at waist height.
C3-06.question: Where do you hit it?

answer.why: With both back, the middle is safest. It gives them no angle, and they hesitate over who takes it.
answer.caption: You finished the weak reply

lo.why: A good idea, but it's hard to drop a waist-high ball short.
lo.caption: They run it down

hi.why: With both back, there's no need to go for the corner. It's a small target and you miss.
hi.caption: Went for the sideline — out

C3-06.coach: Against two players back, go deep down the middle.

C3-07.title: Both opponents up: where to?
C3-07.scene: All four players are at the net.
C3-07.cue: Both opponents are side by side at the net.
C3-07.question: Where do you hit it?

answer.why: When they're both up, the feet in the middle are hardest to handle. Nobody can hit up on it.
answer.caption: It went right between them

lo.why: A good idea, but it's hard to lob deep off a volley.
lo.caption: They turn and get it back

hi.why: Chest height is exactly where a net player likes it.
hi.caption: You gave them chest height

C3-07.coach: When they're both up, hit at the feet down the middle.
C3-07.next: What if a ball comes at your feet?

C3-08.title: A low ball at your partner's feet
C3-08.scene: The opponent's ball drops low at your partner's feet.
C3-08.cue: Your partner gets down almost to one knee.
C3-08.question: What do you do?

answer.why: Your partner's ball will float. One step back and you can handle the ball hit down at you.
answer.caption: You stepped back and held

lo.why: Backing off is right, but that's too far. You barely reach a short volley.
lo.caption: You barely reach it

hi.why: If your partner's ball floats, they'll hit down at the closest feet — yours.
hi.caption: Drilled at your feet

C3-08.coach: When your partner lifts it, you take a step back.
C3-08.next: What if it comes to your feet?

C3-09.title: A ball at your feet: no forcing
C3-09.scene: The opponent's ball drops low at your feet.
C3-09.cue: Their net player is waiting right in front of you.
C3-09.question: Where do you send it?

answer.short: Lift it deep to the back player
answer.why: You have to hit up on a ball at your feet. Avoid the net player and go deep to the back player.
answer.caption: You lifted it deep and held on

lo.short: Drop it short down the middle
lo.why: Okay, but the back player can run in and get it.
lo.caption: They run in and get it back

hi.why: Hitting hard from your feet makes it float — a gift for the net player right in front.
hi.caption: A gift for the net player

C3-09.coach: At your feet: deep, not hard.
C3-09.next: Where do you stand after the block?

C3-10.title: After the low volley: where do you go?
C3-10.scene: You blocked the ball at your feet deep. The opponent takes it from the back.
C3-10.cue: The opponent lifts the low skidding ball.
C3-10.question: Where do you go, and what do you do?

answer.why: They have to lift a deep block. If you close in then, you can finish from above.
answer.caption: You closed in and finished

lo.why: Not bad, but the next ball comes at your feet too.
lo.caption: Another ball at your feet

hi.why: They're pushed back, and if you back off you can't reach the short ball.
hi.caption: It just dropped in front of you

C3-10.coach: If you blocked it deep, the next step is forward.

C3-11.title: A lob over your partner's head
C3-11.scene: The opponent's lob is going deep over your partner's head.
C3-11.cue: Your partner would have to turn their back to see the ball.
C3-11.question: What do you do?

answer.why: You see it from an angle, so you're faster than your partner with their back turned. Chase it and lob it back.
answer.caption: You chased it and lobbed it back

lo.why: Your partner has to run with their back to the net. Even if they get it, it'll be short.
lo.caption: Your partner's ball is short

hi.short: Close in to the middle and watch
hi.why: If you both just watch, nobody chases it.
hi.caption: Nobody chased it down

C3-11.coach: A lob over your partner's head is yours to chase.
C3-11.next: What if your partner smashes it?

C3-12.title: Covering your partner's smash
C3-12.scene: Your partner backs up to smash a lob.
C3-12.cue: Your partner has backed up to the service line.
C3-12.question: Where should you be?

answer.short: Side by side, one step back
answer.why: When your partner hits from back there, a blocked reply comes between you. Side by side, you can cover it.
answer.caption: You finished the blocked reply

lo.why: If the smash is good it's over, but a blocked reply slips between you.
lo.caption: Your partner barely blocks it

hi.why: Move toward your partner and the right opens. The blocked reply goes there.
hi.caption: The right was open

C3-12.coach: When your partner backs up, line up beside them.
C3-12.next: What if you're the one smashing?

C3-13.title: Where to aim your smash
C3-13.scene: The opponents' lob is short. You can smash it.
C3-13.cue: The two opponents are one in front of the other, in the middle.
C3-13.question: Where do you hit it?

answer.why: The front player is closest. Their feet leave the least time to react.
answer.caption: Drilled it at their feet

lo.why: The back player has time to get it. Another lob comes.
lo.caption: Another lob came

hi.short: A sharp angle to the sideline
hi.why: Aiming a smash at the sideline is easy to miss. The target is narrow.
hi.caption: It went out over the sideline

C3-13.coach: Smash at the feet of the closest player.

C3-14.title: Volley exchange
C3-14.scene: All four players are trading volleys at the net.
C3-14.cue: The ball went to the opponent at front left.
C3-14.question: Where do you go?

answer.short: Half a step to the middle
answer.why: The front-left player often goes crosscourt — and that path runs through our middle.
answer.caption: Cut it off in its path

lo.why: The angle down your sideline is narrow. You're half a beat late on a ball through the middle.
lo.caption: Half a beat late

hi.why: Backing off in a volley exchange means you can't reach a short volley.
hi.caption: Beaten by the short volley

C3-14.coach: In volley exchanges too, rotate together toward the ball.

C3-15.title: Volley battle: who breaks first?
C3-15.scene: Your partner's volley landed at the feet of the opponent at front right.
C3-15.cue: The opponent drops the racket close to the ground.
C3-15.question: How will the next ball come?

answer.short: Floating up, in front of you
answer.why: A ball at the feet has to be lifted. In this battle, whoever pops it up first loses.
answer.caption: You hit down on the floater

lo.why: It could, but it's hard to keep it low from their feet.
lo.caption: You got there late

hi.why: They can't hit hard from their feet. If you back off, the floater drops in front of you.
hi.caption: It dropped in front of you

C3-15.coach: In a volley battle, whoever pops it up first loses.

C3-16.title: Between the two — when does it work?
C3-16.scene: One opponent is back; their net player is near the middle of the net.
C3-16.cue: The ball comes at waist height. Not a putaway.
C3-16.question: Where do you hit it?

answer.why: With the net player up, the middle belongs to them. Go deep to the back player.
answer.caption: You kept it away from the net player

lo.why: A good target, but it's hard to place precisely from waist height.
lo.caption: The net player blocks it back

hi.why: With the net player standing there, the middle is easy to poach. It only works when they're level.
hi.caption: Cut off by the net player

C3-16.coach: If their net player is up, the middle belongs to them.
C3-16.next: What if the net player moves to the middle?

C3-17.title: Pulled wide by an angle: where's your partner?
C3-17.scene: An angled (short and wide) volley pulled you out wide to the right.
C3-17.cue: Our front right and middle are open.
C3-17.question: Where does your partner go?

answer.why: When you're out wide, your partner takes the middle. You rotate together toward the ball.
answer.caption: Blocked it in the middle

lo.why: Guarding the left is right, but they'll be late on a ball through the middle.
lo.caption: Your partner barely reaches it

hi.short: Come over to your side too
hi.why: If you're both on the right, the whole left is open. Only come as far as the middle.
hi.caption: The left was open

C3-17.coach: If one gets pulled wide, the other takes the middle.

C3-18.title: Covering the angle, then resetting
C3-18.scene: Your partner covered the middle while you were pulled out by the angle.
C3-18.cue: The ball is coming to you as you go wide.
C3-18.question: Where do you go after hitting?

answer.short: Lob to buy time, then get back
answer.why: A lob buys you time to get back. Your partner moves back to the left.
answer.caption: You got back in position

lo.short: Hit hard and stay out there
lo.why: Hit it hard and it comes back fast. No time to get back.
lo.caption: You barely chase it down

hi.why: Your partner is already in the middle. If you both crowd the middle, the right opens.
hi.caption: Your spot was empty

C3-18.coach: When you're pulled wide, buy time and get back to your spot.
C3-18.next: What if you two are spread apart?

C3-19.title: A poach when they're both up
C3-19.scene: Both opponents are up at the net. You pick off a crosscourt ball.
C3-19.cue: The ball comes at chest height.
C3-19.question: Where do you hit it?

answer.why: With both up, go at the feet down the middle. They leave it to each other and neither gets it.
answer.caption: You finished it between them

lo.why: Not bad, but a ball at the body can be blocked back.
lo.caption: They block it back

hi.short: Hard at the front player's chest
hi.why: Chest height is the easiest ball for a net player. It comes right back.
hi.caption: It came right back

C3-19.coach: On a poach too: both up? Feet, down the middle.

C3-20.title: When to give up the net — the retreat signal
C3-20.scene: Your partner's volley floated high. The opponent is moving under it.
C3-20.cue: The opponent has the racket back behind the head.
C3-20.question: What do you do?

answer.why: A short floater brings a smash. Give up the net and both back off to get it back.
answer.caption: You both backed off and held on

lo.why: Backing off is right, but you're still too close to handle a smash.
lo.caption: You barely got a racket on it

hi.short: Hold your ground at the net
hi.why: Standing at the net makes you the smash target. The closer you are, the less time you have.
hi.caption: The smash went in

C3-20.coach: When the ball floats short, give up the net.
C3-20.next: What if they take the net?

C3-21.title: Their net player moved — the line is open
C3-21.scene: Their net player moved to the middle to cut the ball off.
C3-21.cue: The left sideline where the net player stood is open.
C3-21.question: Where do you hit it?

answer.why: The moment the net player moves, the sideline they left is the nearest open space.
answer.caption: Finished it down the open sideline

lo.why: Safe, but you leave the net player's empty spot alone.
lo.caption: The rally goes on

hi.short: Straight at the net player, middle
hi.why: That's exactly where the net player just moved. It gets cut off.
hi.caption: Cut off in the middle

C3-21.coach: When their net player moves, go down the sideline they left.

C3-22.title: Getting back from a short angle
C3-22.scene: You chased a short angle and got it back from outside on the left.
C3-22.cue: Your partner has moved to the middle.
C3-22.question: Where do you go back to?

answer.short: Diagonally back to your left spot
answer.why: Your partner took the middle. Come back diagonally to the left you left open.
answer.caption: You covered the left again

lo.why: If you stay out there, the front left is open. You barely get there.
lo.caption: You barely reached it

hi.why: Your partner is already in the middle. If you overlap, the whole left is open.
hi.caption: The left was open

C3-22.coach: When you're pulled wide, come back diagonally to your spot.
C3-22.next: What if you two are spread apart?

C3-23.title: Spread apart: who closes first?
C3-23.scene: You're both at the net but spread out to the sidelines.
C3-23.cue: The ball went to the opponent at back left.
C3-23.question: Who closes in first?

answer.why: With the ball on the left, the angles are left and middle. You close the middle first.
answer.caption: You closed the middle

lo.short: Wait for your partner to come
lo.why: Your partner has to guard the sideline. If you wait, the middle stays open.
lo.caption: Your partner barely gets it

hi.why: Backing off while spread out makes the hole even bigger.
hi.caption: Beaten through the middle

C3-23.coach: Whoever is farther from the ball closes the middle first.

C3-24.title: Chapter 3 review — the next move at the net
C3-24.scene: Your partner's volley drove an opponent deep into the left corner.
C3-24.cue: The opponent is stretching, racket face open to the sky.
C3-24.question: How will the next ball come?

answer.why: When the racket face opens in the corner, it's usually a lob. Take a step back and wait.
answer.caption: You smashed the lob

lo.why: They're too stretched to hit hard. Still, you can chase down a lob.
lo.caption: You chase it and barely get it

hi.why: They're set up to lob — if you close in, the space over your head opens.
hi.caption: It went over your head

C3-24.coach: When the racket face opens, wait for the lob.
